locked_story.headline: THE MODEL MADE THE NUMBER
locked_story.one_line: Rainmaker flew two drones through a Kenai Peninsula cloud on August 23 and logged nineteen silver-iodide flare releases. The machines and radar produced a real, auditable trail; the widely repeated nineteen-million-gallon result did not come from a rain gauge. It came from a company model that identified seven radar signatures, removed an assumed background, and converted reflectivity through twenty-seven published relationships into a mean estimate of 57.62 acre-feet, with a much wider stated range.
locked_story.story_question: What did the drones actually measure, and what did the model add?
why_this_one: It is inside the owed window: operation August 23, company validation report August 24.
It has a complete physical chain: two aircraft, nineteen visible releases, flight telemetry, radar signatures, a modeled conversion and a clearly stated uncertainty band.
It is genuinely filmable: a flare becomes a radar streak, then a family of twenty-seven equations becomes one headline-sized volume.

The honest angle is neither boosterism nor debunking. The operation produced observable signatures; the amount of precipitation attributed to it is a company estimate rather than a ground measurement.
It is Alaska-first: the operation took place over the Kenai Peninsula and tests an emerging weather-modification capability in Alaska conditions.

The automation/AI connection is real only at the platform level and must be labeled carefully. The operation used precision drone deployment and Rainmaker describes its broader forecasting/nowcasting stack as data-driven; the specific precipitation estimate is radar modeling, not proof that AI caused rain.

known_source_limits.limit: Company-authored report about the company's own operation; every volume result must remain explicitly attributed as an estimate.
The public list was not available in a form that confirmed or refuted an Alaska activity filing, so the film may not claim either compliance or noncompliance.

The 2025 petition later produced FAA Exemption No. 25287, and a separate altitude waiver was issued August 17, 2026. Those records do not by themselves establish that every condition was met during the Kenai operation, so the film may state the existence of the exemption and waiver but not certify full operational compliance.
